To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimal importance density in a PF is multimodal when the OL is multimodally distributed and the STP is wide.

(i) for multimodal OL problems with broad STP, the optimal importance pdf is unimodal when the STP and the OL are conditionally unimodal on a part of their state vector, (ii) for large-dimensional tracking problems, the optimal importance sampling pdf is unimodally distributed when the state space dimensionality is reduced by a factor of the ratio of the conditional posterior width and the state transition width.
the optimal importance density for PFs is multimodal, and that it is unimodal when conditioned on a small part of the state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the efficiency of PF for two classes of problems: (a) multimodal OLs and (b) large dimensional tracking problems.
developing efficient PFs in two important cases: when the OL is multimodel and the state space dimensionality is large.
developing efficient PFs for problems where either the OL is frequently multimodal/heavy tailed, or the state space dimension (or both) are large.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose a novel particle filtering algorithm for tracking large dimensional state spaces with multimodal observation likelihoods and show that it outperforms existing techniques.
we present a general framework for designing PFs for large dimensional state spaces with multimodal observations and propose two specific techniques which can be applied in many such cases.
the proposed algorithm is an efficient and effective algorithm for tracking spatially varying quantities using a network of spatially distributed sensors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a general framework to handle large dimensional tracking problems with multimodal observation likelihoods.
our techniques can be used to track multimodal OLs with a PF, but with a much reduced computational complexity.
our proposed techniques allow PF to track multimodal OL with a large state space, which is a problem of interest for a wide variety of tracking problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the OL is multimodality is a much stronger indicator for multimodality of the posterior than multimodality of either the STP or the prior.
multimodality of the OL is not an insurmountable problem for PFs, and in fact, multimodality of a part of the posterior can be exploited to improve the accuracy for large dimensional problems.
in large dimensional problems, it may be more efficient to use PFs with a smaller number of particles, but with an importance density that is more complex.
